name: St. Peter
summary: A Galilean fisherman called by Jesus, who named him the rock on which he would build his Church. Leader of the Apostles, he preached in Jerusalem, Antioch and Rome, where he was crucified under Nero.

name: St. Linus
summary: Named by early writers as Peter's first successor in Rome. He may be the Linus greeted by St. Paul in 2 Timothy 4:21.

name: St. Anacletus
summary: Also called Cletus. One of the earliest bishops of Rome, remembered in the Roman Canon of the Mass. Tradition holds that he died a martyr.

name: St. Clement I
summary: Author of the Letter of Clement to the Corinthians, one of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament, urging peace and order in that church.

name: St. Evaristus
summary: An early bishop of Rome during the reign of Emperor Trajan. Little is known for certain about his life; tradition counts him a martyr.

name: St. Alexander I
summary: Led the Roman church in the early 2nd century. Later tradition credits him with introducing the use of blessed water mixed with salt.

name: St. Sixtus I
summary: An early 2nd-century bishop of Rome, remembered among the martyrs. He is often identified with the Sixtus named in early lists of Roman bishops.

name: St. Telesphorus
summary: The first bishop of Rome after Peter whose martyrdom is attested by St. Irenaeus. Tradition links him to the custom of Christmas night Masses.

name: St. Hyginus
summary: Led the Roman church as Gnostic teachers such as Valentinus and Cerdo arrived in Rome, challenging Christian teaching.

name: St. Pius I
summary: Brother of Hermas, author of The Shepherd. During his time the heretic Marcion was expelled from the Roman church.

name: St. Anicetus
summary: Welcomed St. Polycarp of Smyrna to Rome. The two disagreed over the date of Easter but parted in peace and charity.

name: St. Soter
summary: Known for the generosity of the Roman church, which sent aid to Christians in need, praised in a letter by Dionysius of Corinth.

name: St. Eleutherius
summary: Led the Church as the Montanist movement spread. St. Irenaeus wrote of him in his list of Roman bishops.

name: St. Victor I
summary: The first bishop of Rome from North Africa. He pressed churches to celebrate Easter on Sunday, which became the universal practice.

name: St. Zephyrinus
summary: Guided the Church through debates about the Trinity, assisted by his deacon Callixtus, who managed the Christian cemetery on the Appian Way.

name: St. Callixtus I
summary: A former slave who rose to lead the Church. He taught that sinners who repent may be readmitted to communion, and he died a martyr.

name: St. Urban I
summary: Led the Church during a relatively peaceful period under Emperor Alexander Severus.

name: St. Pontian
summary: Exiled to the mines of Sardinia under Emperor Maximinus Thrax, he resigned so the Church could choose a new leader, the first recorded papal resignation.

name: St. Anterus
summary: Reigned only about six weeks. Tradition says he collected the records of the martyrs. He was the first pope buried in the Papal Crypt of the Catacomb of St. Callixtus.

name: St. Fabian
summary: A layman chosen, according to Eusebius, when a dove settled on his head. He organized Rome into districts for the care of the poor and was martyred under Decius.

name: St. Cornelius
summary: Elected after persecution, he welcomed back Christians who had lapsed and repented, opposing the rigorist Novatian. He died in exile.

name: St. Lucius I
summary: Briefly exiled at the start of his reign, he continued Cornelius's merciful policy toward the lapsed. St. Cyprian praised him.

name: St. Stephen I
summary: Taught that baptism by heretics is valid if done in the name of the Trinity, so converts need not be rebaptized, a view later confirmed by the Church.

name: St. Sixtus II
summary: Beheaded with his deacons while celebrating the liturgy in the catacombs during the persecution of Valerian. St. Lawrence was martyred days later.

name: St. Dionysius
summary: Rebuilt the Roman church after the persecution of Valerian and organized parishes. He sent aid to Christians in Cappadocia captured by invaders.

name: St. Felix I
summary: Wrote on the doctrine of the Trinity and the Incarnation. His reign fell under Emperor Aurelian.

name: St. Eutychian
summary: Led the Church in a time of relative peace. Little else is known for certain.

name: St. Caius
summary: Reigned in the years before the Great Persecution under Diocletian. Tradition says he was related to the emperor.

name: St. Marcellinus
summary: Pope at the start of Diocletian's Great Persecution, the most severe the Church endured.

name: St. Marcellus I
summary: Elected after a long vacancy, he reorganized the Roman church after the persecution but was exiled over disputes about readmitting the lapsed.

name: St. Eusebius
summary: Reigned only a few months before being exiled to Sicily by Emperor Maxentius amid unrest over the treatment of the lapsed.

name: St. Miltiades
summary: The first pope of the age of toleration. After the Edict of Milan (313) the empire returned church property, and he received the Lateran palace.

name: St. Sylvester I
summary: Led the Church during the reign of Constantine, when the Council of Nicaea (325) defined the divinity of Christ and the first great Roman basilicas were built.

name: St. Mark
summary: Reigned less than a year. He is credited with founding the Basilica of San Marco in Rome.

name: St. Julius I
summary: Defended St. Athanasius against the Arians and affirmed the faith of Nicaea at the Council of Sardica.

name: Liberius
summary: Exiled by the Arian Emperor Constantius II for refusing to condemn Athanasius. Tradition links him to the founding of St. Mary Major.

name: St. Damasus I
summary: Commissioned St. Jerome to revise the Latin Bible, which became the Vulgate. He honored the martyrs by restoring the catacombs with inscriptions.

name: St. Siricius
summary: Issued the earliest surviving papal decretal, giving binding answers on Church discipline to the bishops of Spain.

name: St. Anastasius I
summary: Condemned certain teachings of Origen. St. Jerome praised him as a man of holy life.

name: St. Innocent I
summary: Pope when Alaric's Visigoths sacked Rome in 410. He firmly asserted Rome's authority and condemned Pelagianism.

name: St. Zosimus
summary: A Greek who at first hesitated over the Pelagian question, then condemned Pelagianism in his letter called the Tractoria.

name: St. Boniface I
summary: His election was contested by the antipope Eulalius. He defended the authority of Rome over the churches of Illyricum.

name: St. Celestine I
summary: Sent bishops to the Council of Ephesus (431), which proclaimed Mary the Mother of God. He sent Palladius to the Christians of Ireland.

name: St. Sixtus III
summary: Rebuilt the Basilica of St. Mary Major to honor Mary as Mother of God after Ephesus, and worked to reconcile the churches of Antioch and Alexandria.

name: St. Leo I (the Great)
summary: His Tome shaped the Council of Chalcedon's teaching that Christ is one person in two natures. He met Attila the Hun and persuaded him to turn back from Rome. A Doctor of the Church.

name: St. Hilarius
summary: As papal legate he had escaped the "Robber Council" of Ephesus. As pope he strengthened Church order in Gaul and Spain and built churches in Rome.

name: St. Simplicius
summary: Reigned when the last Western Roman emperor was deposed in 476. He defended the Council of Chalcedon against the Monophysites.

name: St. Felix III
summary: Excommunicated the Patriarch of Constantinople over the Henotikon, beginning the Acacian Schism between Rome and the East. An ancestor of St. Gregory the Great.

name: St. Gelasius I
summary: Born in Roman Africa, he wrote that the world is governed by two powers, the sacred authority of bishops and the royal power of kings. Known for his charity to the poor.

name: Anastasius II
summary: Sought to heal the Acacian Schism with Constantinople through conciliation.

name: St. Symmachus
summary: Overcame a long challenge from the rival claimant Laurentius. He supported the Catholics of Africa persecuted by the Arian Vandals.

name: St. Hormisdas
summary: Ended the Acacian Schism in 519 with the Formula of Hormisdas, signed by the Eastern bishops. His son later became Pope St. Silverius.

name: St. John I
summary: Sent to Constantinople by the Arian king Theodoric. On his return he was imprisoned at Ravenna, where he died, and he is honored as a martyr.

name: St. Felix IV
summary: Appointed under the influence of King Theodoric. He built the Church of Sts. Cosmas and Damian in the Roman Forum.

name: Boniface II
summary: The first pope of Germanic descent. He confirmed the Council of Orange's teaching on grace against Semi-Pelagianism.

name: John II
summary: The first pope known to have taken a new name on election, since his birth name honored the pagan god Mercury.

name: St. Agapetus I
summary: Traveled to Constantinople, where he deposed the Monophysite patriarch Anthimus and consecrated a successor. He died there.

name: St. Silverius
summary: Son of Pope Hormisdas. He was deposed through the intrigues of Empress Theodora and died in exile. He is honored as a martyr.

name: Vigilius
summary: Held for years in Constantinople by Emperor Justinian during the dispute over the Three Chapters, around the Second Council of Constantinople (553).

name: Pelagius I
summary: Rebuilt the Church's finances and relief of the poor in an Italy devastated by the Gothic Wars.

name: John III
summary: Led the Church as the Lombards invaded Italy. He completed the Church of the Holy Apostles in Rome.

name: Benedict I
summary: Reigned during the Lombard invasions, as famine and plague struck Rome.

name: Pelagius II
summary: Sought help from Constantinople against the Lombards. He died of the plague that swept Rome.

name: St. Gregory I (the Great)
summary: A monk who reluctantly became pope. He sent St. Augustine to convert the English, cared for Rome's poor, reformed the liturgy and wrote the Pastoral Rule. A Doctor of the Church.

name: Sabinian
summary: Successor of Gregory the Great. He sold the Church's grain during a famine, which made him unpopular.

name: Boniface III
summary: Obtained from Emperor Phocas recognition of the Roman church as head of all the churches.

name: St. Boniface IV
summary: Converted the Pantheon in Rome into a church dedicated to Mary and all the martyrs, a step toward the feast of All Saints.

name: St. Adeodatus I
summary: Also called Deusdedit. A Roman priest of long service, he cared for the clergy and the sick during an earthquake and epidemic.

name: Boniface V
summary: Supported the mission to England and corresponded with King Edwin of Northumbria.

name: Honorius I
summary: Promoted missions in England. He was later condemned by the Third Council of Constantinople for his ambiguous letters on Monothelitism.

name: Severinus
summary: His confirmation was delayed more than a year because he refused to accept the Monothelite Ecthesis. He reigned only two months.

name: John IV
summary: A Dalmatian who condemned Monothelitism and ransomed captives taken in his homeland.

name: Theodore I
summary: A Greek from Jerusalem who opposed Monothelitism and excommunicated the Monothelite patriarch Pyrrhus.

name: St. Martin I
summary: Condemned Monothelitism at the Lateran Synod of 649. Arrested by order of Emperor Constans II, he died in exile in Crimea, the last pope honored as a martyr.

name: St. Eugene I
summary: Elected while Martin I was in exile. He stood firm against pressure to accept Monothelitism.

name: St. Vitalian
summary: Sent Theodore of Tarsus as Archbishop of Canterbury, who organized the church in England.

name: Adeodatus II
summary: A Roman monk known for kindness to pilgrims. He restored churches in Rome.

name: Donus
summary: Restored Roman churches and reconciled the church of Ravenna to Rome.

name: St. Agatho
summary: A Sicilian whose letter guided the Third Council of Constantinople (680–681), which condemned Monothelitism.

name: St. Leo II
summary: Confirmed the Third Council of Constantinople. He was noted as a preacher and musician.

name: St. Benedict II
summary: Obtained the emperor's agreement that a pope could be consecrated without waiting for imperial approval.

name: John V
summary: The first of a series of Eastern popes of this era, born in Syria. He was known for his generosity.

name: Conon
summary: An elderly compromise candidate, son of a soldier from Thrace. He reigned less than a year.

name: St. Sergius I
summary: Introduced the Agnus Dei into the Mass, refused to accept the decrees of the Council in Trullo, and baptized King Caedwalla of Wessex.

name: John VI
summary: A Greek who ransomed captives taken by the Lombards and protected Rome.

name: John VII
summary: A Greek who decorated Roman churches with fine mosaics and frescoes.

name: Sisinnius
summary: Suffered severely from gout and reigned only about three weeks.

name: Constantine
summary: The last pope to visit Constantinople before Paul VI in 1967, where he was received with honor by Emperor Justinian II.

name: St. Gregory II
summary: Commissioned St. Boniface as missionary to the Germans and opposed Emperor Leo III's iconoclasm.

name: St. Gregory III
summary: Born in Syria, the last pope to seek the Byzantine emperor's approval. He condemned iconoclasm and supported St. Boniface's missions.

name: St. Zachary
summary: The last Greek pope of the period. He approved Pepin's anointing as King of the Franks and negotiated peace with the Lombards.

name: Stephen II
summary: Crossed the Alps to seek Frankish help against the Lombards. Pepin's donation of land laid the foundation of the Papal States.

name: St. Paul I
summary: Brother of Stephen II. He strengthened the alliance with Pepin and moved relics from the catacombs into Rome's churches.

name: Stephen III
summary: Held the Lateran Council of 769, which set rules for papal elections and condemned iconoclasm.

name: Adrian I
summary: Allied with Charlemagne, who defeated the Lombards. His legates took part in the Second Council of Nicaea (787), which restored the veneration of icons.

name: St. Leo III
summary: Crowned Charlemagne emperor on Christmas Day 800, founding the Holy Roman Empire.

name: Stephen IV
summary: Traveled to Reims to crown Louis the Pious as emperor.

name: St. Paschal I
summary: Built and decorated churches in Rome, including Santa Prassede, and gave refuge to Greek monks fleeing iconoclasm.

name: Eugene II
summary: Accepted the Constitutio Romana, defining the emperor's role in Rome. He promoted education for clergy.

name: Valentine
summary: A Roman deacon praised for his piety. He died after a reign of about a month.

name: Gregory IV
summary: Tried to mediate in the civil wars of Louis the Pious and his sons. He fortified Ostia against Saracen raids.

name: Sergius II
summary: Reigned when Saracen raiders sacked St. Peter's Basilica outside the walls of Rome in 846.

name: St. Leo IV
summary: Built the Leonine Wall around St. Peter's and the Vatican after the Saracen raid, and led the defense of Rome at the Battle of Ostia.

name: Benedict III
summary: His election was briefly challenged by the antipope Anastasius. He worked to help churches in England and the East.

name: St. Nicholas I (the Great)
summary: A strong pope who upheld the indissolubility of marriage against King Lothair II and asserted papal authority in the dispute over Patriarch Photius.

name: Adrian II
summary: Approved the Slavonic liturgy of Sts. Cyril and Methodius. His legates attended the Fourth Council of Constantinople.

name: John VIII
summary: Defended Rome against Saracen raids and supported St. Methodius. He was the first pope to be assassinated.

name: Marinus I
summary: Had served as papal legate to Constantinople. He was the first pope known to have been bishop of another diocese before his election.

name: St. Adrian III
summary: Reigned about a year amid factional violence in Rome. He died on his way to an imperial diet.

name: Stephen V
summary: Fed Rome during famine and drought. He forbade the Slavonic liturgy after Methodius's death.

name: Formosus
summary: A former missionary to Bulgaria. After his death his body was exhumed and put on trial by Stephen VI in the infamous "Cadaver Synod."

name: Boniface VI
summary: Reigned only about two weeks amid the turmoil after Formosus's death.

name: Stephen VI
summary: Held the Cadaver Synod against Formosus's corpse. Public outrage led to his imprisonment and death.

name: Romanus
summary: Reigned about four months during the turbulent years after the Cadaver Synod.

name: Theodore II
summary: In a reign of about twenty days, he reburied Formosus with honor and restored those he had ordained.

name: John IX
summary: Confirmed the rehabilitation of Formosus and annulled the Cadaver Synod.

name: Benedict IV
summary: Crowned Louis III of Provence as emperor. He was praised for his charity.

name: Leo V
summary: Overthrown after about a month and imprisoned. He likely died in prison.

name: Sergius III
summary: Reigned at the start of the period when Rome's aristocratic families dominated the papacy. He rebuilt the Lateran Basilica after an earthquake.

name: Anastasius III
summary: Reigned about two years while the powerful Theophylact family controlled Rome.

name: Lando
summary: Reigned about seven months. His name has never been used by another pope.

name: John X
summary: Organized the Christian alliance that defeated the Saracens at the Garigliano (915). He was deposed and died in prison.

name: Leo VI
summary: Reigned about seven months while Marozia controlled Rome.

name: Stephen VII
summary: Reigned about two years under the influence of Marozia. He granted privileges to monasteries.

name: John XI
summary: Son of Marozia, elected young. He granted privileges to the reforming Abbey of Cluny.

name: Leo VII
summary: Supported monastic reform and invited St. Odo of Cluny to Rome.

name: Stephen VIII
summary: Reigned under the domination of Alberic II, ruler of Rome.

name: Marinus II
summary: Concentrated on the reform of clergy and monasteries.

name: Agapetus II
summary: Supported monastic reform and the expansion of the Church in Germany and Scandinavia.

name: John XII
summary: Became pope as a teenager. He crowned Otto I emperor in 962, but his worldly life led Otto to have him deposed.

name: Leo VIII
summary: A layman installed by Emperor Otto I. His status was disputed, but he is counted in the official list.

name: Benedict V
summary: Elected by the Romans after John XII's death, he was deposed by Otto I and died in exile in Hamburg.

name: John XIII
summary: Crowned Otto II co-emperor and established new dioceses, including Magdeburg as a center for missions to the Slavs.

name: Benedict VI
summary: Murdered in prison by order of the Crescentii family.

name: Benedict VII
summary: Restored order in Rome, opposed simony and supported monastic reform.

name: John XIV
summary: Chancellor of Emperor Otto II. After Otto died, he was imprisoned and died in the Castel Sant'Angelo.

name: John XV
summary: Carried out the first recorded formal canonization, of St. Ulrich of Augsburg, in 993.

name: Gregory V
summary: The first German pope, a cousin of Emperor Otto III, elected in his mid-twenties.

name: Sylvester II
summary: The first French pope and the greatest scholar of his age, who promoted mathematics and astronomy. He established the church in Poland and Hungary, sending a crown to St. Stephen.

name: John XVII
summary: Reigned about six months under the Crescentii family.

name: John XVIII
summary: Founded the Diocese of Bamberg. He retired to a monastery near the end of his life.

name: Sergius IV
summary: Known as a generous pope who cared for the poor during famine.

name: Benedict VIII
summary: Crowned St. Henry II emperor and held synods against clerical marriage and simony.

name: John XIX
summary: A layman, brother of Benedict VIII, who was elected and ordained in one day. He crowned Conrad II emperor.

name: Benedict IX (1st time)
summary: A young member of the Tusculum family whose scandalous life led to his expulsion from Rome. He is the only man to serve as pope three separate times.

name: Sylvester III
summary: Briefly installed after Benedict IX was driven out, then removed when Benedict returned.

name: Benedict IX (2nd time)
summary: Returned briefly, then resigned the papacy in exchange for money to his godfather, who became Gregory VI.

name: Gregory VI
summary: Paid Benedict IX to resign, hoping to reform the Church. Accused of simony at the Synod of Sutri, he stepped down.

name: Clement II
summary: A German bishop appointed after the Synod of Sutri. He crowned Henry III emperor and held a synod against simony.

name: Benedict IX (3rd time)
summary: Seized Rome a third time after Clement II's death but was driven out by the emperor's forces.

name: Damasus II
summary: A German bishop who died about three weeks after his consecration.

name: St. Leo IX
summary: Launched the Gregorian Reform, traveling widely to hold synods against simony. His legates' clash with Constantinople in 1054 marked the East-West Schism.

name: Victor II
summary: A German counselor of Henry III who continued the reform program.

name: Stephen IX
summary: Former abbot of Monte Cassino who supported the reformers, including St. Peter Damian.

name: Nicholas II
summary: Decreed in 1059 that popes would be elected by the cardinals, the foundation of the modern conclave.

name: Alexander II
summary: Continued the reform with the help of Hildebrand and blessed the Norman conquest of England.

name: St. Gregory VII
summary: The great reformer who fought simony and lay investiture. His conflict with Emperor Henry IV led to the emperor's penance at Canossa in 1077.

name: Bl. Victor III
summary: A great abbot of Monte Cassino who rebuilt its basilica. He reluctantly accepted the papacy.

name: Bl. Urban II
summary: A French Cluniac monk who called the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in 1095.

name: Paschal II
summary: Continued the investiture struggle. He was imprisoned by Henry V and forced into concessions he later revoked.

name: Gelasius II
summary: Driven from Rome by the emperor's forces. He died in exile at Cluny.

name: Callixtus II
summary: Ended the Investiture Controversy with the Concordat of Worms (1122) and called the First Lateran Council (1123).

name: Honorius II
summary: Approved the Premonstratensian order and the Rule of the Knights Templar.

name: Innocent II
summary: Overcame the schism of antipope Anacletus II with St. Bernard's support and called the Second Lateran Council (1139).

name: Celestine II
summary: A student of Peter Abelard, he reigned less than six months.

name: Lucius II
summary: Struggled against the Commune of Rome. He died from wounds suffered in an attack on the Capitol.

name: Bl. Eugene III
summary: A Cistercian disciple of St. Bernard of Clairvaux, who preached the Second Crusade at his request.

name: Anastasius IV
summary: An elderly Roman who made peace with the Roman commune and Emperor Frederick Barbarossa.

name: Adrian IV
summary: The only English pope. He crowned Frederick Barbarossa and had earlier served as legate to Scandinavia.

name: Alexander III
summary: A great canon lawyer who defeated Barbarossa's antipopes, canonized St. Thomas Becket and called the Third Lateran Council (1179), which required a two-thirds vote to elect a pope.

name: Lucius III
summary: Issued the decree Ad abolendam against heresy at the Council of Verona in 1184.

name: Urban III
summary: Opposed Emperor Frederick Barbarossa. He died shortly after news of the fall of Jerusalem.

name: Gregory VIII
summary: Called the Third Crusade after Saladin captured Jerusalem. He reigned less than two months.

name: Clement III
summary: Made peace with the Roman commune, allowing the popes to return to Rome, and supported the Third Crusade.

name: Celestine III
summary: Became pope at about 85. He crowned Henry VI emperor and approved the Teutonic Knights.

name: Innocent III
summary: The most powerful medieval pope. He approved St. Francis's first rule and called the Fourth Lateran Council (1215), which taught on the Eucharist and annual Confession.

name: Honorius III
summary: Approved the Dominicans (1216), the Franciscan Rule (1223) and the Carmelite Rule. He promoted the Fifth Crusade.

name: Gregory IX
summary: Friend of St. Francis, whom he canonized. He published the Decretals, a major collection of Church law, and established the papal Inquisition.

name: Celestine IV
summary: Elected under harsh conditions imposed by a Roman senator. He died about two weeks later.

name: Innocent IV
summary: A canon lawyer who called the First Council of Lyon (1245) and gave the cardinals their red hats.

name: Alexander IV
summary: Protected the mendicant orders and canonized St. Clare of Assisi.

name: Urban IV
summary: Son of a French shoemaker. He established the feast of Corpus Christi in 1264, for which St. Thomas Aquinas wrote hymns.

name: Clement IV
summary: A French lawyer and widower who became a priest. He asked Roger Bacon to send him his scientific writings.

name: Bl. Gregory X
summary: Elected after a three-year vacancy. He called the Second Council of Lyon (1274), which briefly reunited East and West and created the rules of the conclave.

name: Bl. Innocent V
summary: The first Dominican pope, a theologian and colleague of St. Thomas Aquinas in Paris.

name: Adrian V
summary: Died about five weeks after election, before he could be ordained a priest.

name: John XXI
summary: The only Portuguese pope, a physician and logician. He died when a ceiling collapsed in his palace at Viterbo.

name: Nicholas III
summary: A Roman noble who began moving papal residence to the Vatican and clarified the Franciscan rule of poverty.

name: Martin IV
summary: A French pope closely allied with Charles of Anjou.

name: Honorius IV
summary: A Roman noble who supported the Carmelites and Augustinian hermits and encouraged the study of Eastern languages.

name: Nicholas IV
summary: The first Franciscan pope. He sent missionaries to China and rebuilt St. Mary Major.

name: St. Celestine V
summary: A holy hermit elected after a two-year deadlock. Overwhelmed, he resigned after five months, and later died in confinement.

name: Boniface VIII
summary: Declared the first Holy Year (Jubilee) in 1300. His bull Unam Sanctam asserted papal supremacy during his conflict with King Philip IV of France.

name: Bl. Benedict XI
summary: A Dominican who sought peace with France after Boniface VIII's death.

name: Clement V
summary: A Frenchman who settled the papacy at Avignon. He called the Council of Vienne, which suppressed the Knights Templar.

name: John XXII
summary: An able administrator at Avignon who canonized St. Thomas Aquinas in 1323.

name: Benedict XII
summary: A Cistercian who defined that the souls of the just see God immediately after death (Benedictus Deus). He began the Palace of the Popes at Avignon.

name: Clement VI
summary: Bought Avignon for the papacy. During the Black Death he cared for the sick and protected Jews from blame.

name: Innocent VI
summary: Reformed the Avignon court and sent Cardinal Albornoz to restore order in the Papal States.

name: Bl. Urban V
summary: A Benedictine who briefly returned the papacy to Rome (1367–1370) and founded universities.

name: Gregory XI
summary: Urged by St. Catherine of Siena, he returned the papacy to Rome in 1377, ending the Avignon period. He was the last French pope.

name: Urban VI
summary: His harsh manner led French cardinals to elect an antipope months later, beginning the Western Schism.

name: Boniface IX
summary: Roman pope during the Western Schism. He restored papal control over Rome.

name: Innocent VII
summary: Roman pope during the Schism. He restored the University of Rome.

name: Gregory XII
summary: Resigned at the Council of Constance in 1415 to help end the Western Schism. He was the last pope to resign until Benedict XVI.

name: Martin V
summary: Elected at the Council of Constance, ending the Western Schism. He restored Rome and the Papal States.

name: Eugene IV
summary: Called the Council of Florence, which briefly reunited the Greek and Latin Churches in 1439.

name: Nicholas V
summary: The first Renaissance pope. He founded the Vatican Library and planned the rebuilding of St. Peter's.

name: Callixtus III
summary: Organized defense against the Ottomans after the fall of Constantinople and ordered the retrial that cleared St. Joan of Arc.

name: Pius II
summary: A famous humanist writer. He died at Ancona while preparing a crusade against the Ottomans.

name: Paul II
summary: A Venetian who built the Palazzo Venezia in Rome. He set the Jubilee every 25 years.

name: Sixtus IV
summary: A Franciscan who built the Sistine Chapel and reopened the Vatican Library, but was marked by nepotism.

name: Innocent VIII
summary: Reigned as the Renaissance papacy became heavily involved in Italian politics.

name: Alexander VI
summary: The notorious Borgia pope, whose worldly life became a symbol of Renaissance corruption. He drew the line dividing new lands between Spain and Portugal.

name: Pius III
summary: Nephew of Pius II. He reigned only 26 days.

name: Julius II
summary: The "Warrior Pope." He laid the cornerstone of the new St. Peter's Basilica and commissioned Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel ceiling and Raphael's frescoes.

name: Leo X
summary: A Medici patron of the arts. He excommunicated Martin Luther in 1521 as the Protestant Reformation began.

name: Adrian VI
summary: A Dutch reformer and the last non-Italian pope until John Paul II. He publicly admitted the failings of the Roman Curia.

name: Clement VII
summary: Pope during the Sack of Rome (1527) and King Henry VIII's break with Rome over his marriage. He commissioned Michelangelo's Last Judgment.

name: Paul III
summary: Opened the Council of Trent (1545), approved the Jesuits (1540) and condemned the enslavement of Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

name: Julius III
summary: Reopened the Council of Trent and named Michelangelo architect of St. Peter's.

name: Marcellus II
summary: A reformer who reigned only 22 days. Palestrina's famous Missa Papae Marcelli is named for him.

name: Paul IV
summary: Co-founder of the Theatines, a severe reformer who created the Index of Forbidden Books.

name: Pius IV
summary: Brought the Council of Trent to its close in 1563, assisted by his nephew St. Charles Borromeo.

name: St. Pius V
summary: A Dominican who put Trent's reforms into effect, issued the Roman Catechism, Breviary and Missal, and called Christendom to pray the Rosary before the victory at Lepanto (1571).

name: Gregory XIII
summary: Introduced the Gregorian calendar in 1582, still used worldwide, and founded colleges including the Gregorian University.

name: Sixtus V
summary: A Franciscan who reorganized the Roman Curia into congregations, fixed the cardinals at 70 and completed the dome of St. Peter's.

name: Urban VII
summary: Reigned 13 days, the shortest papacy in history. He is remembered for an early public smoking ban.

name: Gregory XIV
summary: A friend of St. Philip Neri who reigned less than a year.

name: Innocent IX
summary: An experienced diplomat who reigned about two months.

name: Clement VIII
summary: Reconciled King Henry IV of France to the Church and issued the revised Clementine Vulgate.

name: Leo XI
summary: A Medici who reigned 27 days.

name: Paul V
summary: Completed the façade of St. Peter's Basilica, which bears his name. He canonized St. Charles Borromeo.

name: Gregory XV
summary: Founded the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith to direct missions and canonized Sts. Ignatius, Francis Xavier, Teresa of Ávila and Philip Neri.

name: Urban VIII
summary: Consecrated the new St. Peter's (1626) and commissioned Bernini's baldacchino. Galileo was tried during his reign.

name: Innocent X
summary: Condemned the five propositions of Jansenism and commissioned Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.

name: Alexander VII
summary: Commissioned Bernini's colonnade around St. Peter's Square and welcomed Queen Christina of Sweden into the Church.

name: Clement IX
summary: A poet and librettist known for his charity. He brokered the "Clementine Peace" with the Jansenists.

name: Clement X
summary: Became pope at almost 80. He canonized St. Rose of Lima, the first saint of the Americas.

name: Bl. Innocent XI
summary: A reforming pope who organized the Holy League that saved Vienna from the Ottomans in 1683.

name: Alexander VIII
summary: Condemned Gallican claims against papal authority. He bought valuable manuscripts for the Vatican Library.

name: Innocent XII
summary: Banned nepotism with the bull Romanum decet Pontificem (1692) and cared for the poor.

name: Clement XI
summary: Condemned Jansenism in the bull Unigenitus and made the Immaculate Conception a feast for the whole Church.

name: Innocent XIII
summary: Ordered the Jesuits to stop accepting novices during the Chinese Rites controversy.

name: Benedict XIII
summary: A devout Dominican who kept living as a friar and continued pastoral work as pope.

name: Clement XII
summary: Built the Trevi Fountain and the façade of St. John Lateran, and first condemned Freemasonry (1738).

name: Benedict XIV
summary: A scholarly pope who set the modern rules for canonization and promoted science and learning.

name: Clement XIII
summary: Defended the Jesuits against expulsions by European kings and promoted devotion to the Sacred Heart.

name: Clement XIV
summary: A Franciscan who, under pressure from Catholic monarchs, suppressed the Society of Jesus in 1773.

name: Pius VI
summary: Pope during the French Revolution. Napoleon's armies seized the Papal States, and he died a prisoner in France.

name: Pius VII
summary: Signed the Concordat of 1801 with Napoleon and was later imprisoned by him. He restored the Jesuits in 1814.

name: Leo XII
summary: Promoted strict moral reform in the Papal States and proclaimed the Holy Year of 1825.

name: Pius VIII
summary: A canon lawyer who reigned 20 months. During his reign Catholics in Britain received civil rights.

name: Gregory XVI
summary: A Camaldolese monk who strongly promoted missions and condemned the slave trade in 1839.

name: Bl. Pius IX
summary: The longest papacy after St. Peter. He defined the Immaculate Conception (1854), called the First Vatican Council, which defined papal infallibility, and lost the Papal States in 1870.

name: Leo XIII
summary: Founded modern Catholic social teaching with Rerum Novarum (1891) on workers' rights, revived the study of St. Thomas Aquinas and wrote the Prayer to St. Michael.

name: St. Pius X
summary: A pastor at heart who allowed children to receive Communion from age seven, encouraged frequent Communion, revived Gregorian chant and opposed Modernism.

name: Benedict XV
summary: Worked tirelessly for peace and relief of prisoners during World War I and promulgated the first Code of Canon Law (1917).

name: Pius XI
summary: Signed the Lateran Treaty (1929), creating Vatican City. He established the feast of Christ the King and condemned Nazism in Mit brennender Sorge.

name: Ven. Pius XII
summary: Led the Church through World War II, sheltering many Jews in Church buildings. He defined the Assumption of Mary in 1950.

name: St. John XXIII
summary: Good Pope John surprised the world by calling the Second Vatican Council (1962) and wrote Pacem in Terris on peace.

name: St. Paul VI
summary: Guided the Second Vatican Council to its close, carried out its reforms, became the first pope to travel by plane to six continents and wrote Humanae Vitae.

name: Bl. John Paul I
summary: The smiling pope, the first to take a double name. He died 33 days after his election.

name: St. John Paul II
summary: The first Polish pope. He traveled to 129 countries, helped bring down communism in Europe, began World Youth Day and issued the Catechism of the Catholic Church.

name: Benedict XVI
summary: A great theologian who wrote the Jesus of Nazareth books and encyclicals on love and hope. He became the first pope in nearly 600 years to resign.

name: Francis
summary: The first pope from the Americas and the first Jesuit pope. He emphasized mercy and care for the poor, wrote Laudato Si' on creation and led the Synod on Synodality.

name: Leo XIV
summary: The first pope from the United States, born in Chicago. An Augustinian, he served for years as a missionary and bishop in Peru before leading the Dicastery for Bishops.
